traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and formal requirements from docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md are implemented and validated:
- Core Functionality & REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG: `valid-annotation-format` supports nested and flat configurable patterns via `story.pattern`/`req.pattern` and `storyPathPattern`/`requirementIdPattern`, wired through `valid-annotation-options.ts` and exercised by multiple dedicated tests. - Backward Compatibility & REQ-BACKWARD-COMPAT: When no custom patterns are configured, or when configured patterns are invalid, the rule falls back to the original hardcoded defaults for both story paths and requirement IDs, as verified by the *FALLBACK* tests. - Pattern Validation & REQ-REGEX-VALIDATION: Patterns are compiled with `new RegExp(...)` under try/catch; invalid regex sources generate stable configuration errors and default back, as asserted by tests covering invalid nested and flat pattern options. - Error Messages & REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES: Optional `storyPathExample` / `requirementIdExample` (and nested `story.example` / `req.example`) are resolved with clear precedence and used in error messages; tests confirm custom examples appear and that nested examples override flat ones. - Schema & Quality Standards & REQ-SCHEMA-VALIDATION: The rule’s JSON schema defines all new options with correct types, disallows unknown properties, and is hooked via `meta.schema`; configuration tests validate this behavior. - Integration & REQ-CONSISTENCY: Default patterns align with the `valid-story-reference` rule’s expectations, and both rules’ tests pass together, demonstrating consistent behavior and non-conflicting configuration. - REQ-PATTERN-TESTING: Pattern resolution and validation logic are factored into shared helpers and comprehensively exercised by the dedicated `valid-annotation-format` test suite.
Given the direct story linkage in tests, passing targeted and full test runs, verified implementation in helper and rule files, and up-to-date documentation, this story is fully implemented and validated.
